setting: You all work the same ambulance crew out of a Toronto EMS station, covering calls across the city. You've been crewing together long enough to have seen each other at your worst and your best, and you spend off-shift time the same way most EMS crews do — decompressing over bad food and worse jokes. You all knew a colleague who recently died, someone from the station or the broader Toronto EMS community.
openers: tell them Ortiz's send-off turned into the strangest call he's ever run
rank the top five worst smells they've collectively encountered on shift
propose a formal competition for who had the worst call this month
remind them of the time Ortiz somehow made a code brown funny

private_lines.Shane: You live in a rented place in Scarborough, split between EMS shifts and security contractor work, and you live alone.
private_lines.Kayla: You live in a shared apartment near Danforth while juggling your paramedic shifts and nursing school coursework.

situation: Three paramedics on the same crew, off shift.
topic: Competing to tell the grimmest, most disgusting call-out stories with the blackest jokes they can manage, including the death of someone they all knew, joked about because nobody can cope otherwise.

text:
so I need to tell you both what happened today

---Fri 18:15, Shane

at Ortiz's thing
okay so you know how they had the reception at the legion on Lawrence
I know the one. I had to leave early, what happened.
so around 2:30 when they're doing the toasts, one of his uncles just goes down
like full collapse, face down into the buffet table
takes half the cold cuts with him
he's fine, vasovagal, he's 70 and hadn't eaten and had two rye and ginger in like 20 minutes
me and Fernandez from 54 are the only medics in the room who are off duty so we go over
and we're both in dress clothes, there's no equipment, we're doing a full assessment on this man on the floor of the legion with cold cuts everywhere
she came over and held his hand while we were with him and she said "Miguel always said you people never stop working"
and then she went and got us both a plate
That sounds exactly like something she would do.
the uncle is sitting up eating perogies by the time the truck gets there
Fernandez had to give a statement to the crew who showed up and explain why two off-duty medics were already on scene at a memorial reception
the look on that poor PCP's face when he walked in and figured out whose reception it was
don't know them, 42 unit I think
Ortiz would have found that very funny.
I kept thinking that the whole time
like he would have been absolutely losing it
Remember when he showed up to Delaney's retirement party and Delaney's dad coded and they had to call it in
I'll try. Might be late, Diane has something going on with the car.
we'll be there for a while
Stuck here, go ahead without me.
Paul you missed Kayla's story about the guy with the garden hose
she was going to tell you anyway
I've been a medic for 22 years, I already know how that ends.
It was a full 30 footer paul
